title: Social Programme
text: On Tuesday evening, 22 September 2026, the social event takes place at the Riegele Wirtshaus, the brewery tavern of Brauhaus Riegele in the centre of Augsburg. It starts at 18:30. See the Programme for the full schedule of the day.

title: Social Programme
text:
Getting there
The programme of the day ends at 18:00 and the evening event starts at 18:30, so we will head to the restaurant directly after the last session.
We will leave from the workshop venue as a group at about 18:00. From the venue, take tram line 3 towards Augsburg Hauptbahnhof from the stop Innovationspark/LfU (about a 3-minute walk east of Building W) and stay on it to the terminus Augsburg Hauptbahnhof. From there the Wirtshaus is roughly 250 m away, a three-minute walk.
Please buy your own tram ticket, either in the DB Navigator app or at a ticket counter (Ticketschalter). The ticket is the only thing you will need to pay for yourself. Everything else is covered, though.

title: Social Programme
text:
Brewery tour
The evening will open at 18:30 with a guided tour of the Riegele brewery, followed by dinner at the Wirtshaus. Brauhaus Riegele traces its roots back to the brewery Zum Goldenen Ross, first documented in 1386, and has been run by the Riegele family since 1884.

title: SciML Frontiers: Progress, Evolution, and Future Directions — Workshop 2026
text:
22–23 September 2026 • Augsburg, Germany



Scientific Machine Learning (SciML), the fusion of scientific computing and machine learning algorithms, has proven to be a transformative force in academia and is rapidly establishing a firm foothold in industrial applications. The foundational 2018 SciML workshop outlined six priority research directions (PRDs) for the nascent field of SciML, anchoring future development around critical pillars such as domain awareness, robustness, and interpretability. The SciML landscape has evolved profoundly over the past seven years. Considering these advancements, this workshop, hosted by the Centre for Advanced Analytics and Predictive Sciences at the University of Augsburg, convenes researchers from diverse disciplines to re-evaluate the original priorities within the context of current technological frontiers. Through an expert keynote, technical presentations, and collaborative breakout sessions, participants will share practical insights and critically analyse current progress and emerging challenges within the field. Our primary objective is to assess the trajectory of the original PRDs and collaboratively shape the future research agenda for SciML. The insights generated during this two-day event will be synthesised into a comprehensive scientific article, targeting high-impact journals such as Nature Machine Intelligence or Neurocomputing.
We have synthesised the original six PRDs into four focused research directions, which participants will explore deeply during the breakout sessions.





Numerical Foundation of SciML


Discretisation, Stability and Convergence







Beyond prediction


Control, Optimisation and Application







Automation and Scalability in SciML


From Prototype to Production Scale







Domain Awareness and Interpretability


Physical Priors, Explainability and Trust




The event is organised by Prof. Lars Mikelsons, Prof. Michael Schlottke-Lakemper and Andreas Hofmann (see Organisers), and is hosted by the Centre for Advanced Analytics and Predictive Sciences at the University of Augsburg.

title: Programme
text:
Session types
The programme combines an invited keynote, contributed presentations, and collaborative breakout sessions:

The Keynote fills a 60-minute slot — a speaker introduction, a 45-minute presentation and time for questions — and sets the stage for the workshop.
Presentations are contributed talks of 15 minutes plus 5 minutes for questions.
Breakout sessions are the core of the workshop. They run in four parallel tracks, one per research direction, with the goal of critically assessing progress since the original priority research directions and identifying open challenges. The track overview introduces the four tracks, and participants sign up for the track they would like to join.
Presentation of breakout findings brings the groups back together to report their results to all participants.
Organisational and collaborative slots — track overview, track sign-up, status sync, final result preparation, and the evening event — are used to coordinate between the groups and to prepare the joint outcome of the workshop.

The findings collected during the breakout sessions form the basis of the joint scientific article that will be prepared after the workshop.

title: Publication
text:
The insights generated during this two-day event will be synthesised into a comprehensive scientific article, targeting high-impact journals such as Nature Machine Intelligence or Neurocomputing.
The article will be written collaboratively after the workshop and will build on the results of the four breakout sessions. All participants are invited to contribute as authors.
